items.title: Icing Encounter
items.failure_mode: Inadvertent encounter with structural icing conditions (visible moisture + OAT below freezing).
items.effect: Ice accumulation on wings and tail can increase stall speed by 15-30% and reduce control effectiveness.
items.cause: Flight continued into icing conditions in an aircraft that is NOT certified for flight into known icing (FIKI).
items.mitigation: Pitot heat; immediate 180° turn or descent

items.title: Alternator Failure in IMC
items.failure_mode: Alternator failure while in instrument meteorological conditions (IMC).
items.effect: The essential bus provides 30 min of power — sufficient for an approach at a nearby airport but requiring prompt action.
items.cause: Alternator mechanical or electrical fault (belt, regulator, or windings).
items.mitigation: Essential bus isolation; battery endurance ≥ 30 min

items.title: Carbon Monoxide Incapacitation
items.failure_mode: CO leaking into cabin via exhaust muff cracks.
items.cause: Exhaust muff cracks; CO binds to haemoglobin with 200× the affinity of oxygen.
items.mitigation: Active CO detector per AD 2024-01-05; muff inspection

items.title: G1000 Display Overheat
items.failure_mode: PFD or MFD display failure due to excessive cockpit temperatures.
items.effect: Loss of primary flight or navigation displays; reversionary mode retains partial function.
items.cause: Direct sunlight on ramp, >50°C / 122°F cockpit.  The G1000 operating temperature specification is −20°C to +55°C.

items.title: Fuel Exhaustion in Flight
items.failure_mode: Fuel mismanagement or undetected leak leading to fuel exhaustion before destination.
items.effect: Engine stoppage with no fuel remaining.  Leading cause of general aviation accidents (approximately 8% of all GA accidents per AOPA Nall Report).
items.cause: Inaccurate fuel planning, or a leak that goes undetected between pre-flight inspections.
items.mitigation: Fuel totalizer on G1000 MFD; pre-flight dipstick check

items.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff
items.failure_mode: Loss of engine power during takeoff below 500 ft AGL.
items.effect: Forced landing straight ahead or within 30° of heading.  Cessna 172's low stall speed (48 KIAS clean) and benign stall characteristics make survivable outcomes highly probable if the pilot maintains airspeed.
items.cause: Engine mechanical or fuel/ignition failure despite pre-flight checks (e.g. magneto or fuel-system fault).
items.mitigation: Pre-takeoff run-up check; engine trend monitoring
